newsitem.title: USA: General Acceptance declared in default.
newsitem.headline: General Acceptance declared in default.

text.p: General Acceptance Corp, a sub-prime auto lender, on Friday said its primary creditor has declared the company in default under the terms of its $70 million revolving line of credit.
As a result, the interest rate under the line of credit increased to 6.5 percent over the one-month London Interbank Offered Rate from 4.5 percent over one-month LIBOR, the company said.
The action was prompted by General Acceptance continuing to be out-of-compliance with certain financial covenants as a result of its first-quarter loss, the company said.
The lender is continuing to fund the company on a daily basis while both parties attempt to work out a mutually acceptable resolution, General Acceptance said.
The company reported a net loss of $7.7 million, or $1.28 a share, in the first quarter.
General Acceptance shares were unchanged at 3-3/8 Friday.
